# What you get

Files land in `./ig_archiver/` in whatever directory you run from, one
subfolder per account. Move them wherever you like afterwards, or point
somewhere else with `--out`.

```text
ig_archiver/
  archive.log
  someaccount/
    2026-08-17_DcJvpIRjwJa_01.jpg
    2026-08-17_DcJvpIRjwJa_02.mp4
    2026-07-08_DZsluBdCreP_01.jpg
    metadata/
      index.csv      index.json      one row per file
      posts.csv      posts.json      one row per post
      comments.csv   comments.json   if --comments was used
      followers.csv                  one row per followers run
      followers/2026-08-27_2050.json a dated snapshot of the names
```

Each account owns its records. They sit in `metadata/` rather than among the
pictures, so a file browser opened on the account folder shows photographs and
nothing else, and two accounts never share a file.

Photos and videos share one numbering sequence per post, in carousel order. A
file's number is its position in the post, not a running count of what a
particular run downloaded - so a photo keeps the same name whether or not
videos were saved alongside it.

## Flat or nested

Flat is the default. `--nested` gives each post its own folder:

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Flat (default)

```text
someaccount/
  2026-08-17_DcJvpIRjwJa_01.jpg
  2026-08-17_DcJvpIRjwJa_02.jpg
```

### `--nested`

```text
someaccount/
  2026-08-17_DcJvpIRjwJa/
    01.jpg
    02.jpg
```

:::

Switching layout does not re-download anything.
[`relayout`](commands.qmd#relayout) moves what is already there and updates the
index; folders left empty are tidied up. A run that only changes layout
reports `Files downloaded: 0`.

## The index

`metadata/index.csv` and `index.json` are **merged, never overwritten**. Each
run loads the existing index, skips anything already recorded, appends the new
rows and rewrites both files.

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `post_url` | canonical post URL |
| `username` | account that posted it |
| `post_id` | Instagram's shortcode |
| `post_date` | the post's own date |
| `media_type` | `image`, `video` or `video_skipped` |
| `carousel_index` | position within the post |
| `filename` | file on disk |
| `relative_path` | path relative to the output directory |
| `source_url` | CDN URL it came from |
| `sha256` | hash of the bytes |

Re-running is safe: hashes are loaded from the index first, so files already on
disk are never downloaded twice.

## The post list

`metadata/posts.csv` and `posts.json`, written by
[`scan`](commands.qmd#scan) and by archiving runs - one row per post.

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `post_url`, `post_id` | the post, and Instagram's shortcode |
| `username` | account that posted it |
| `post_date`, `post_time` | its date, and the exact timestamp when the page gave one |
| `kind` | `post` or `reel` |
| `likes` | like count - [a lower bound when read as a viewer](visibility.qmd#like-counts) |
| `views` | play count, reels only, [account itself only](visibility.qmd#view-counts) |
| `comments` | comment count |
| `images`, `videos`, `media_count` | what the post holds |
| `caption` | the caption text |

## Comments

`--comments` writes `metadata/comments.csv` and `comments.json`:

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `post_url`, `post_id`, `post_date` | the post they belong to |
| `account` | the account whose post it is |
| `username` | who wrote the comment |
| `timestamp` | when, ISO 8601 |
| `text` | what they wrote |

Comments are read from the rendered page - Instagram's page JSON leaves
`preview_comments` empty even on a post with 4,193 - so only what the page has
loaded is captured, which is a handful on a busy post.

## Followers

[`followers`](commands.qmd#followers) writes a dated snapshot of the names to
`metadata/followers/` and appends one row per run to `metadata/followers.csv`:

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `taken_at` | when the snapshot was taken |
| `count` | names actually collected |
| `stated_count` | the follower count Instagram displayed |
| `complete` | whether those two matched |
| `joined`, `left` | change since the previous **complete** snapshot |

## Placeholders

Without `--videos`, a carousel slide that held a video would leave a silent
gap: the numbering jumps and nothing records that anything was there. A
placeholder image is written instead.

```text
someaccount/
  2026-08-17_DcJvpIRjwJa_01.jpg
  2026-08-17_DcJvpIRjwJa_02.video-not-saved.png     <- a video was here
  2026-08-17_DcJvpIRjwJa_03.jpg
```

It is a plain grey PNG, so it sorts into the right position in any photo
browser and is obviously not a photograph. The index records it with a
`media_type` of `video_skipped`, which is how
[`fill-videos`](commands.qmd#fill-videos) finds it later.

## File dates

Each saved file's modified time is set to **when the post was made**, not when
you downloaded it, so the archive sorts chronologically in any file browser.
Instagram strips EXIF from uploads, so the filesystem timestamp is the only
honest place to record this.

## Encoding

CSV and log files are written with a byte-order mark. Excel and PowerShell 5.1
otherwise read a CSV as the legacy Windows codepage, which turns Icelandic and
every other non-ASCII caption into mojibake. The content is ordinary UTF-8
either way.
